details:
It was discovered that SSVNC incorrectly handled certain CoRRE rectangles,
leading to a heap buffer overflow. A malicious VNC server could possibly
use this issue to cause SSVNC to crash, resulting in a denial of service,
or possibly execute arbitrary code. (CVE-2018-20020)

It was discovered that SSVNC incorrectly handled certain raw rectangles,
leading to an infinite loop. A malicious VNC server could possibly use this
issue to cause SSVNC to consume excessive resources, leading to a denial of
service. (CVE-2018-20021)

It was discovered that SSVNC did not properly initialize certain messages
sent to the server. A malicious VNC server could possibly use this issue to
obtain sensitive information. (CVE-2018-20022)

It was discovered that SSVNC did not check for memory allocation failures
in its zlib and ZRLE decoders, leading to a NULL pointer dereference. A
malicious VNC server could possibly use this issue to cause SSVNC to crash,
resulting in a denial of service. (CVE-2018-20024)
